newsitem.title: CANADA: TVX says maximum Q4 charge is US$57 mln.
newsitem.headline: TVX says maximum Q4 charge is US$57 mln.

text.p: TVX Gold Inc officials said on Monday that the maximum fourth-quarter charge for shutting down the company's Casa Berardi gold mine in Quebec would be US$57 million.
"The worst scenario is US$55 million plus reclamation," which would total up to an extra US$2 million, spokesman Ed Baer said in an interview.
The book value of the mine was US$55 million, but TVX may be able to sell the property to reduce its losses, Baer said.
"We have expressions of interest from a couple of parties," he said.
He would not say how much the company expected to gain from a sale.
Production at Casa Berardi was about 75,000 ounces in 1996, of which TVX's share was about 44,000 ounces, said Cliff Davis, the company's new senior vice-president of North American operations.
The rest went to TVX's joint venture partner at the project, Vancouver-based Golden Knight Resources Inc.
The shutdown of Casa Berardi would not interfere with TVX's promise to shareholders to produce one million ounces of gold a year by the year 2000, said Davis.
Expected growth at the company's Greek operations would more than make up for the loss of Casa Berardi, Davis said.

The company has been taking a serious second look at all its operations over the past six months. In September, TVX shut down its operations at Mineral Hill in Montana because of high costs and low grades.
The company said it decided to shut down Casa Berardi because of high costs and dwindling reserves.
But production at the New Britannia gold mine in Manitoba was stable, Davis said.
The 300 employees at Casa Berardi were to be told of the shutdown decision this afternoon, he said.
